newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Only two-week renwal proposed for U.N. Angola force.
newsitem.headline: Only two-week renwal proposed for U.N. Angola force.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan recommended on Tuesday only a two-week renewal of the U.N. peacekeeping force in Angola, until April 15, because of continuing uncertainty over the date when a national unity government would be inaugurated.

The 6,240-strong force, called the U.N. Angola Verification Mission III (UNAVEM III), was most recently renewed for a month, until March 31, while previous mandates have usually been for two or three months.
The shorter periods enable the Security Council to keep the situation under closer scrutiny.

Establishment of a national unity government, originally scheduled for Jan. 25 but repeatedly postponed, would mark the culmination of a 1994 accord ending nearly two decades of civil war between the government of Angolan President Jose Eduardo dos Santos and UNITA, the former rebel movement.
The Security Council recently threatened UNITA with trade and travel sanctions if it continued to delay the formation of a unity government.

In a report to the council reflecting talks held during a just-completed visit to Angola, Annan again said the delay was "primarily because UNITA did not send to Luanda those of its officials who have been designated to join the National Assembly and the new government."
But he said his visit and meetings with dos Santos and UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi "give rise to expectations that new vigour can be injected into the peace process."

"The resolution of the future status of the UNITA leader and the promise of Mr. Savimbi to send to Luanda the rest of the UNITA National Assembly deputies and additional designated officials with a view to establishing the government of unity and national reconciliation are encouraging signs," he said.
"If these commitments are fulfilled, I am confident that it will be possible to establish the government of unity and national reconciliation in the very near future," he added.
"Final and courageous steps need to be taken by the two parties and their leaders in order to complete the peace process expeditiously."

Annan, who flew to Togo on Tuesday for an African summit meeting focusing on the crisis in Zaire, said he would provide a more detailed assessment of his visit to Angola on his return to U.N. headquarters on March 31.

"In the meantime, given the uncertainty concerning the exact date for the inauguration of the government of unity and national reconciliation, I recommend that the Security Council consider extending the mandate of UNAVEM III for two weeks only, until April 15, 1997," he said.
